trap-nonspeakable.notes: THREE FINDINGS, none fixed inline. (1) T(2,4) IS NOT A KNOT. The block writes 'The knot T(2,4) carries [4]_q' and calls the pair a 'torus-knot pair'. T(p,k) is a knot iff gcd(p,k) = 1; gcd(2,4) = 2, so T(2,4) is the (2,4)-TORUS LINK with TWO components — the closure of sigma_1^4 in B_2, which is the standard 2-component (4,2) link, not a knot. The companion pair it is compared to, {T(2,9), T(3,5)}, is genuinely two knots (gcd 1 both), which makes the slip easy to miss. The same issue affects 'the lepton tower T(2,k)', which is a knot only for odd k. (2) THE LEAN PATTERN LOOKS SELF-ASSUMING. The block describes MesonGMORFactorization as 'the substrate factorisation axiom' and then says meson_ratio_via_alpha_shift 'proves the factorisation using the specific indices'. If the class carries the factorisation as a field and the theorem projects it, that is the vacuous self-assuming projection AGENTS.md section 3b-cond item 5 forbids — the class must axiomatise the HYPOTHESES, not the conclusion. Worth checking QOU.BraidKnot.meson_ratio_via_alpha_shift directly. (3) NUMBER SUPPLIED (the block quotes none): at the proton pin, [3]_q [4]_q = 12.50866587 against (m_K/m_pi)^2 = 12.51120685 from PDG m_K+- = 493.677, m_pi+- = 139.57039, i.e. -203.1 ppm. Note this disagrees with the sibling prop:meson-kaon-pion-hecke-seifert, whose route gives -289.65 ppm on the unsquared ratio (about -579 ppm squared): two derivations of the same observable in one chapter, differing by roughly 3x in residual. Also the .ts has uses: [] while the .md cites prop:alpha-shift-torus-knot, so the dependency edge is missing.
